title: `sum` of floats: pairwise, Kahan when grouped
verdict: pairwise (full); Kahan (grouped, in memory); in turn (grouped, streaming); in the input's width
description: A full aggregation sums pairwise: blocks of 128 in 16 SIMD stripes, combined pairwise, the remainder added in turn. Groups of indices use Kahan summation with a finiteness guard. Streaming merges partial sums plainly.
The sum of no values (or only nulls) is 0 in the Series API.

The sum has the input's width. A `Float32` column adds in single precision on every path: `sum_arr_as_f32` with `f32` lanes, `KahanSum<f32>` per group, `NumSumReducer<Float32Type>` (`SumCast` maps `f32` to `f32`). One `Float32` group of 16777216, 1, 1 sums to 16777216 ungrouped and grouped when streaming, and to 16777218 grouped in memory (Kahan). Each step is one IEEE addition, rounded to nearest with ties to even; the paths differ in the order of the additions. The float-sum kernel uses plain `+`, not the reassociable `alg_add_f64`.

Streaming engine (a lazy `collect()` by default, polars-exec-engine): ungrouped, each morsel is summed by the in-memory kernel (`ChunkAgg::sum`, pairwise per chunk), added to its pipeline's running sum, and the pipelines' sums are added in pipeline order. Which morsels a pipeline receives depends on scheduling, so the grouping of a large sum can change between runs. Grouped, each value is added in turn to its group's sum (`reduce_one`, `+=`) and the pipelines' partial sums are added on merge. So grouped sums differ between the engines: Kahan in memory, plain left-to-right when streaming. One `Float64` group of 1e16, 1, 1, -1e16 sums to 2.0 in memory and 0.0 streaming.

Order class (in memory): (a) ungrouped, pairwise with blocks of 128: in a block each of 16 lanes adds its 8 values in turn and the lanes reduce in a tree of depth 4, the blocks combine pairwise, and the first n mod 128 values are added in turn and then to the rest; several chunks add their sums in turn. Grouped by index groups, Kahan's compensated sum in the input's width with the error kept only while finite; grouped by slices (sorted keys), the ungrouped kernel per slice. (b) Any tree: |ŝ − s| ≤ γ_h Σ|x_i| (Higham §4.2), h ≤ max(12 + ⌈log₂ B⌉, r) for one array of n = 128B + r values (7 lane additions, 4 lane levels, ⌈log₂ B⌉ pairwise levels, the final addition; r for the leading remainder); for n ≥ 2¹⁶ that is about ⌈log₂ n⌉ + 5, below the sequential n − 1. Kahan: (2u + O(nu²)) Σ|x_i| (§4.3). u = 2⁻⁵³ for `Float64`, 2⁻²⁴ for `Float32`, which sums in `f32` throughout. (c) The source below; polars-sum-float's manual repros (16777218 and 2.0 grouped in memory). (d) Ungrouped and slice-grouped: ANY (a fixed tree), never SEQUENTIAL past 128 values. Index-grouped Kahan: no Lean order (duckdb-kahan-sum has a four-value Kahan result outside every tree sum). `Float32`: no Lean order either, as `SumOrder` rounds every step to a double; the class is ANY at u = 2⁻²⁴. The in-memory planner can also hand a group_by with at most two plain column keys and sum/mean/min/max/first/last/count aggregations to the streaming group-by (`partitionable_gb`, when it has a streaming builder); the probes saw Kahan in memory, so that branch was not taken there.
reference: `AggFn.fsum` (`floatSum`) adds the doubles one by one in list order from +0.0; the writers that need that order exactly use `Dialect.float_sum`. NULL without values.

provenance.notes: Polars 2.1.0 (Python) from the project's environment, macOS arm64, `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=2`; each `LazyFrame` collected with `engine="in-memory"` and `engine="streaming"`.

notes: Narrowed to the in-memory engine; the streaming engine, which sverify targets, is in polars-sum-float-streaming. The streaming probes show a grouped sum adding in turn (0.0 and 16777216 where memory gives 2.0 and 16777218) and an ungrouped sum that varies between runs.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.
